what_happened: The job "Route checks by job kind per ci-routing section 3.2" (20261017-044557-3htd) ended failed at admission, before any work was done. Admission refused it because athena.toml is a governance file. A job may change that file only if the accepted reading lists it as a deliverable and names it in an acceptance criterion. This reading did not. The event lists no acceptance criteria, blocker or major findings, or failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Routing checks by job kind is configuration, so the outcome inherently needs an athena.toml edit. But the step that turns a request into a reading does not look at which files the outcome will touch, and it does not compare them with the governance-protected list. The protection rule is only enforced at admission, after the reading has been accepted and the job submitted. So a gap in the reading shows up as a refused job, not as a correction made while the reading is drafted.
prevention: Add a check when the reading is drafted or accepted. It would work out which files the request's outcome is likely to touch, for example any request mentioning routing, checks, classes or budgets, and compare them with the governance-protected list. If a protected file such as athena.toml is likely to change, the check would require it to appear as a named deliverable and in an acceptance criterion, or send the reading back for revision before the job is submitted. This would cover the whole class, not just athena.toml.
proposed_request: Route checks by job kind as described in ci-routing section 3.2. The change needs an edit to athena.toml, so the reading must list athena.toml as a deliverable. It must also name athena.toml in an acceptance criterion that states the intended behavior: each job kind runs the checks that section 3.2 assigns to it. Check this by running representative jobs of each kind and confirming that the checks run match section 3.2. If the config schema needs a change to accept the new routing fields, make it in the same change, and confirm that athena.toml parses with the schema in the committed tree.
